answer.label: Written by
answer.sourceLine: Margaret Atwood wrote this in chapter 10 of The Handmaid’s Tale (1985). It is part of Offred’s fictional narration about life before Gilead, not an independently recorded speech by Atwood.

author.bio: Margaret Atwood is a Canadian novelist, poet and critic whose fiction explores power, gender and the stories people tell about themselves. Her novels include The Handmaid’s Tale, The Robber Bride and the Booker Prize-winning The Blind Assassin.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Offred remembers a time when disturbing news could be treated as something happening elsewhere, outside the routines of ordinary life. The distinction makes ignoring an active refusal of attention, which is why critics debate whether the passage confesses complicity as well as describing vulnerability.
